advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the tightened/line-anchored shared patterns do not regress workflow-file secret detection (esp. inline PEM headers and short tokens), or keep lint's broader shapes for the raw-text sweep.
evidence: Old lint patterns (removed): `re.compile(r"\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}\b")`, `re.compile(r"\bsk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}\b")`, `re.compile(r"https://hooks\.slack\.com/services/[A-Za-z0-9/]+")`, `re.compile(r"-----BEGIN [A-Z0-9 ]*PRIVATE KEY-----")`
New shared table: src/rebar/secret_screen.py:79 `gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}`, :91 `sk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{24}`, :109 slack webhook `{40}`, :99 PEM anchored `^\s*-----BEGIN ...-----\s*$`
src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint.py:64: `for label, m in iter_line_matches(line):` now drives entirely off the shared, stricter table
advisory.finding: Migrating lint.secret_scan onto the shared SECRET_PATTERNS table narrows workflow-file secret detection: the old table matched looser/shorter shapes (gh[pousr]_{20,}, sk_live_{16,}, Slack webhook [A-Za-z0-9/]+, unanchored PEM header), while the shared table demands full live lengths, applies an entropy floor, and line-anchors the PEM header. Shorter tokens and inline (mid-line) PEM headers that the old lint caught will no longer be flagged in workflow files.
scenarios: A workflow file embedding a PEM private-key header on a line with other content (e.g. `key: "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----..."`)
A workflow file embedding a Stripe key of 16-23 body chars or a short Slack webhook path

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update user-guide's screened-family list to include the 'URL with an inline password' family present in SECRET_PATTERNS.
evidence: docs/user-guide.md: 'screened for live credential shapes (Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, Google, Atlassian, Slack, AWS, PyPI, Stripe, PEM private keys)'
src/rebar/secret_screen.py: '("URL with an inline password", re.compile(r"\b[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://[^\s:/@]+:[^\s:/@]{8,}@[^\s/@]+"), False),'
advisory.finding: The user-guide enumerates the screened credential families as '(Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, Google, Atlassian, Slack, AWS, PyPI, Stripe, PEM private keys)', but the code's SECRET_PATTERNS table additionally defines a 'URL with an inline password' family (and a distinct 'Slack webhook URL' family), so the documented list understates what the screen actually refuses.
scenarios: An operator hits a refusal on a body containing a `user:password@host` URL and finds no matching family in the documented list, making the refusal appear undocumented/unexpected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add 'URLs with inline passwords' (and confirm the Slack webhook family) to the parenthetical family list in docs/user-guide.md.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-grep in test_the_inbound_jira_translate_routes_through_the_shared_seam with a behavioral call to _write_event_file(...) asserting CommandError and that no event file lands when the Jira body carries a synthetic credential.

assert "_seam.finalize_event(" in source

advisory.finding: test_the_inbound_jira_translate_routes_through_the_shared_seam asserts on the SOURCE TEXT of inbound_translate.py (`_seam.finalize_event(` present, `_seam._apply_authorship(` absent) instead of exercising the routing. This is source-grepping the code under test: it breaks on a rename of finalize_event or a reformat with no behavior change, and never runs the screen — a regression where the seam is called but no longer screens, or a revert to a direct call that still refuses, is not what the grep pins. The reconciler's `_write_event_file(tracker_dir, ticket_id, event_type, data)` is directly callable, so a behavioral test can pass a Jira comment body carrying a synthetic credential and assert CommandError is raised and no event file lands.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the exact-source-text pin `rebar.comment(ticket_id, body)` with a signature-based check that `allow_secret_pattern` is absent from every MCP tool function's parameters (inspect.signature), which survives refactors of the call site.
evidence: assert "rebar.comment(ticket_id, body)" in inspect.getsource(_mcp_writes)
_mcp_writes.py:151-153 `def comment_ticket(ticket_id: str, body: str) -> str: ... rebar.comment(ticket_id, body)` — the pinned string is the exact call text under test
docstring: 'MCP tool schemas are derived from the tool functions' signatures' — a signature-based assertion is the behavioral contract
advisory.finding: test_the_override_is_not_exposed_over_mcp asserts `"rebar.comment(ticket_id, body)" in inspect.getsource(_mcp_writes)`, pinning the exact source text of the call. This is a change-detector: renaming the `body` parameter, reformatting the call across lines, or otherwise refactoring without altering the published tool schema would break the test even though the override remains unexposed. The test's own docstring states the schema is derived from the tool functions' SIGNATURES, so inspect.signature over the tool functions is the behavioral contract to assert, not the call's source text.
advisory.suggested_fix: Iterate the mcp tool functions and assert 'allow_secret_pattern' not in inspect.signature(fn).parameters, rather than grepping the call's source text.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the inbound Jira reconcile path's new CommandError-on-secret behavior (inbound_translate.py:276 → _write_event_file → apply_inbound_records.py:542) is the intended contract and that a mirror that fails has a recovery path, since the `--allow-secret-pattern` override is CLI-only and unreachable from the reconciler.
evidence: inbound_translate.py:276 `_seam.finalize_event(event, ticket_id, event_type, data, str(tracker_dir), _repo_root)` replacing the prior direct `attribution_fields` + `_apply_authorship` calls
_seam.py:354 `screen_event(data)` runs inside finalize_event and _seam.py:395 `raise CommandError(...)` on a live-shaped credential
apply_inbound_records.py:542 `path = _write_event_file(tracker_dir, local_id, "COMMENT", event_data)` — no surrounding try/except in `_inbound_update_apply_comments`
apply_inbound.py:166 `_inbound_update_apply_comments(payload, tracker_dir, local_id, written)` propagates to `_apply_inbound_update` with no CommandError handling
applier.py:725 `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — per-mutation failure backstop (records + continues)` is where the new CommandError is ultimately absorbed

Contrast: apply_inbound_records.py:311 `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail-open: skip comment bootstrap` wraps the CREATE-path comment write at line 337, so the two COMMENT-writing paths now behave differently on the same input
advisory.finding: Routing inbound Jira translate through `finalize_event` (inbound_translate.py:276) adds a new `CommandError` raise path to `_write_event_file`, changing the inbound-comment contract: a Jira comment carrying a live-credential shape that previously ALWAYS wrote a local COMMENT event now fails its mutation. The inbound-UPDATE comment path (`_inbound_update_apply_comments`, apply_inbound_records.py:542) has no local handler and relies on the applier's per-mutation backstop (applier.py:725) to record-and-continue, unlike the CREATE-bootstrap comment path (line 337) which sits inside its own fail-open try/except (line 311). Same producer emitting COMMENT events, divergent consumer behavior on a body that used to be accepted.
scenarios: A Jira issue receives a comment quoting a credential (e.g. an AWS example key or a PEM header on its own line); the inbound reconcile pass now fails that comment's mutation and records a backstop error instead of mirroring it locally
An operator syncing an existing external ticket whose description/comments were previously mirrored verbatim sees inbound comments silently dropped-with-error rather than applied

blocking.finding: secret-detection: a deterministic secrets/security detector matched 2 location(s) on changed file(s): src/rebar/secret_screen.py, tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py. Remediate the match, or allowlist a confirmed false positive.

bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 502 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug e7a9-35fa-1d58-4095 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan e7a9-35fa-1d58-4095` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review e7a9-35fa-1d58-4095` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan e7a9-35fa-1d58-4095 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.

evidence: src/rebar/_io/import_ndjson.py:229: `local = create_ticket(repo_root=rr, **_provenance.create_kwargs(rec))`
src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:354: `screen_event(data)` runs inside finalize_event for every append_event write, and screen_event reads the `_secret_override` contextvar which the importer never sets

The commit message claims the importer 'reaches the store WITHOUT append_event' but import_ndjson uses the public write API which funnels through append_event/finalize_event; the importer therefore inherits the screen with no bypass
The follow-up ticket 4802 notes the reconcile-fails-loudly case but does NOT mention the bulk-import abort case
dropped.finding: The NDJSON bulk importer routes its writes through create_ticket/comment/edit_ticket -> append_event -> finalize_event -> screen_event, but never enters a forced_secret_write scope and the public create_ticket/edit_ticket/comment library entrypoints used by the importer expose no allow_secret_pattern override. A single imported record whose body/description contains a live-shaped credential now raises CommandError and aborts the entire bulk import mid-flush, with no operator recourse.
scenarios: Bulk-importing historical Jira/NDJSON data where any comment or description quotes a doc example key (e.g. AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE) or a real credential
A long import fails partway through a chunk flush, leaving a partial import
